cells.title: Tell a project at onboarding when its deploy drives no product first
cells.action: Implement docs/history/deploy-verify-gate/CONTEXT.md D5 as refined by D6, and contract C1. Anchors in onboard/notices.rs: `pub fn stale_advisor_notices(repo_root: &Path) -> Vec<String> {` and, inside it, the verification arm that pushes `VERIFICATION_UPKEEP_POINTER.to_string()` or one of the two verification offers; in onboard/templates.rs: `pub const VERIFICATION_UPKEEP_POINTER` (the voice to follow). Add a predicate over the repo root that reads only docs/DEPLOY.md and scripts/deploy.sh (a missing or unreadable file counts as absent, never a panic) and is true when at least one of them exists and any one that exists lacks the text `.bee/verify/verify-app/` (D7). When it is true, push one notice, a new constant in templates.rs, right after the whole verification arm and before the design offer, whichever branch of that arm ran, the retired-verify-key branch included (D7: it is a separate fact). The notice says, in plain words: this project's deploy goes live without driving the product first; before the first live step, its deploy record and script should run the full product drive of its verify skill and stop on a failure; use the bee-deploying skill to add that step; when the project has no verify skill yet, the bee-verifying skill builds one. It writes nothing and refuses nothing. Every other notice stays byte-identical. Red first, with test names that contain deploy_verify: docs/DEPLOY.md without the path fires once; scripts/deploy.sh that names `.bee/verify/verify-app/control-x` while docs/DEPLOY.md is absent is silent; docs/DEPLOY.md naming the path while scripts/deploy.sh lacks it fires; no deploy file is silent; a project with only scripts/release.sh is silent; the retired verify key present with a deploy file lacking the path fires; and the existing verification notice tests still pass unchanged. The knowledge delta is left to dvg-3; this cell writes no docs. No code comments. The proof run must show the new tests ran: quote the count of tests the filter matched, which must be above zero.
cells.verify: cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --bin bee -- deploy_verify && cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --bin bee -- every_code_file_is_at_or_below_its_comment_baseline

truths: A project with docs/DEPLOY.md or scripts/deploy.sh where any existing one lacks .bee/verify/verify-app/ gets one notice that its deploy drives no product first
A project whose every existing deploy file names .bee/verify/verify-app/ gets no such notice
A project with no deploy file, or only scripts/release.sh, gets no such notice
Every other onboarding notice is unchanged

cells.title: Make every bee-written deploy drive the product before going live
cells.action: Implement docs/history/deploy-verify-gate/CONTEXT.md D1, D2, D3 and D4, as refined by D7, in three skills and two templates. Load the bee-technical-writing skill first. (1) references/deploy.sh.template: add a `--skip-product-drive` flag beside `--yes` and `--allow-dirty` (anchor: `YES=0; ALLOW_DIRTY=0`) and to the usage line (D7 b). Add a step between the test step (anchor: `echo "== test"`) and the deploy step (anchor: `echo "== deploy $ENV_NAME $VERSION"`): it finds the files matching `.bee/verify/verify-app/control-*`; exactly one: run it with bash and the arguments `drive --full`; exit 0 goes on; exit 2 stops with a message that the control script has no `drive --full` entry point and that the bee-verify-upkeep skill adds it; any other non-zero exit stops with a message that the product drive went red and nothing went live (the flag never overrides a red drive); none: stop with a message that the project has no verify skill and that the bee-verifying skill builds one, unless --skip-product-drive was passed, in which case print that the product was not driven and go on; more than one: stop and name them. Keep `set -euo pipefail` semantics, write no comments in the template, and prove it in a scratch copy under .bee/tmp with its angle-bracket placeholders replaced by harmless commands: bash -n, then four runs against fake control scripts that exit 0, 1 and 2 and against no control script (with and without the flag), each showing the expected go-on or stop. Record those runs in the cap. (2) references/DEPLOY.template.md: in `## Steps`, add a SAFE row before the first LIVE row that runs `bash .bee/verify/verify-app/control-<app> drive --full` and must show every feature ok; add one sentence under the table that this row is the product drive and the `## Verify` section is the check of the live target after the deploy. (3) SKILL.md of bee-deploying: in Branch A, add a step before the Preconditions step: check that the record and the script carry the product drive step before the first LIVE step; when either lacks it, add it to both in the same turn from the templates and report the edit; check, by reading the control script (never by a full run), that it answers `drive --full`, and when it does not, point to bee-verify-upkeep before running anything LIVE; when the project has no verify skill, say so and point to bee-verifying. When the deploy is owned by a project release script or deploy skill (Step 0), do not edit it: tell the user the drive step is missing and ask (D7 e). In B4, say the record and script carry the drive step. In Hard rules, add that `--skip-product-drive` is the user's choice for one run, never the agent's, the same as `--yes`, and that it never overrides a red drive. Renumber steps where needed. (4) SKILL.md of bee-verifying, section 5: give the full drive its literal entry point `drive --full` beside the fast one, and state the exit-code contract: one ok or FAIL line per mapped feature; exit 0 when every one passes, 1 when any fails, 2 when the entry point is unknown; a deploy script reads that exit code before it goes live (D7 c). (4b) SKILL.md of bee-verify-upkeep: in its Pass, add one step that checks the control script answers `drive --fast` and `drive --full` with that exit-code contract, and adds a missing one, proven by running it (D7 d). (5) Run `.bee/bin/bee dev regen` so the rendered copies and the release manifest match the sources; never hand-edit a rendered copy. Cite CONTEXT.md D-numbers in prose, never raw decision ids. One commit.

bee-verifying section 5 names drive --full and its 0, 1, 2 exit-code contract
The rendered skill copies match their sources after the regen chain
deploy.sh.template gives exit 2 of the drive its own message pointing to bee-verify-upkeep
bee-verify-upkeep checks and adds the drive --fast and drive --full entry points
